chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, from Abu Baseer, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who looked at the leg of a woman and discharged semen. He (peace be upon him) said: 'If he was wealthy, then upon him is a camel; and if he was in between (wealth levels), then a cow; and if he was poor, then a sheep. Indeed, I did not make that upon him because of the water (semen), but because he looked at what was not permissible for him.'
ai.seo_question: What is the compensation for looking at a woman's leg and discharging semen according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the financial penalty (kaffarah) for a man in Ihram who gazes at a woman's leg and discharges semen is rooted in the violation of the gaze itself, rather than the resulting seminal emission. The compensation scales with the individual's financial capacity—camel, cow, or sheep—demonstrating the Shia jurisprudential principle of proportionality in expiation. This highlights the significance of 'ghurrah al-basar' (the glance) as a distinct sin requiring atonement, even if the physical act of ejaculation is secondary to the visual transgression.
